blocks.value: Communication Design is all about creating visual strategies and eye-catching design narratives to communicate with people and convey important information or messages through the intervention of media, ensuring satisfactory user experiences. Students get exposure to a variety of fields within the domain of Communication Design, such as graphics & publications, visual storytelling, brand identity and promotion design, information design, and more.

Communication Design Courses are provided in different specializations which are Graphic Design, Web Design, UI & UX Design, Information Design, Motion Graphics and Animation, Game Design, etc. Motion Graphics, Advertising, Web Design, Social Media Design, Graphic Design, Exhibition Design all come under the umbrella of Communication Design . BDes Communication Design , MDes in Communication Design , Certificate in Communication Design , Diploma in Communication Design are some of the Courses provided in Communication Design in top communication Design Colleges such as NIFTs, Pearl Academy, Symbiosis Institute of Design, Amity University, JD Institute of Fashion Technology, World University of Design. After the completion of this course, Communication Design graduates can choose their career paths among Graphic Designer, Multimedia Artist, Art Director, Web Designer, Visual Designer, Animator, Creative Director, Brand Manager, Game Designer and can easily earn INR 4 LPA - INR 6 LPA .
To learn more about Communication Design in detail , read the article below.

faqs.question: What is Communication Design course all about?
faqs.answer: The demand for communication designers are increasing day-by-day . A communication designer's job is to create a connection between the spectator and the visuals. A communication design course will teach students everything they need to know to become expert communication designers. faqs.question: Is there any age limit to apply for Communication Design courses?
faqs.answer: No, usually there is no minimum or maximum age limit to apply for Communication Design courses . However, some colleges may have their own eligiblity parameters. If you want to pursue BDes in Communication Design then you should be not be older than 21 years. However, if you wish to pursue BA Communication Design, BSc Communication Design or MDes Communication Design then there is no age limit.

faqs.question: Can I pursue postgraduate-level Communication Design course after BTech?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can apply for postgraduate-level Communication Design courses such as MA Communication Design , MSc Communication Design and MDes Communication Design after completing BTech. Make sure that you have passed the degree with at least 50% marks or 5.5 CGPA. Hope this helps!!!

salary.title: Communication Design: Salary, Career Scope, Job Profiles, and Top Recruiters

blocks.value: Design courses allow students to use their creativity and expand their career growth. The process of communication and information has changed swiftly, causing a wave of change in the academic sector as well. Communication design has developed swiftly because it operates in fields such as media, software, games, publishing, advertising, and public relations, all of which are needed in our everyday lives, whether they are real or virtual.

The communication design programme has a wide range of professional opportunities with an original approach, and many startups hire communication designers for their online websites, designs, and other projects.  Other job titles include design thinking expert, industrial designer, interior designer, and user experience designer.

questions.question_text: Which is more difficult, NIFT or NID DAT?

answers.answer_text: NIFT and NID are equally tough. NIFT has two stages: NIFT Written exam and NIFT Situation Test and Personal Interview, whereas NID DAT also has two stages: NID DAT Prelims and NID Mains, which include Studio test and Personal Interview. Candidate who is preparing for NIFT can give NID DAT entrance exam with the same preparation. Practice and consistency in required for both exams.
